long.title: Field Notes, Episode 31: The tide pools between the first light and the returning water
long.creator: Dr. Imani Cole
long.description: Imani returns to the same stretch of rocks across three low tides, comparing the creatures visible before sunrise with those that appear when the water begins to warm. The episode follows a small pool from its deepest shadow to the first wave that reconnects it with the sea. Along the way she explains why visitors should watch from the dry rock, leave shells where they find them, and give the birds room to feed.

one.author: Dana
one.text: The tide pool section is the best twenty minutes of the series.

long.author: Dr. Imani Cole from the Riverside Coastal Field Research Station
long.text: The species list includes the common shore crab, beadlet anemone and several kinds of periwinkle. I added notes on which animals were visible at each tide because the same pool looked quite different before sunrise. The episode notes also include the survey dates and the field guide we used to distinguish young shore crabs from the smaller swimming crabs. Please leave the animals in the water if you visit the site yourself.
